The second season of the American [[adult animated]] [[Superhero fiction|superhero]] series ''[[Invincible (TV series)|Invincible]],'' based on the [[Invincible (comics)|comic book series of the same name]], was created for television by comic book writer [[Robert Kirkman]] who also wrote the comics. The season was produced by [[Amazon MGM Studios]] in association with [[Point Grey Pictures]], [[Skybound Entertainment#Subsidiaries|Skybound North]], Skybound Animation and Wind Sun Sky Entertainment, with Simon Racioppa serving as [[showrunner]]. Taking place a month after the events of the previous season, Mark Grayson is attempting to regain his life after being betrayed by [[Omni-Man]] while simultaneously dealing with the repercussions of the aftermath and attempting to not end up like his father. Also, Mark contends with a new threat in [[Angstrom Levy]], an interdimensional traveler with a personal vendetta against him.

[[Steven Yeun]] stars as [[Invincible (character)|Mark Grayson / Invincible]], while [[Sandra Oh]] and [[J. K. Simmons]] play his parents [[Debbie Grayson]] and [[Omni-Man|Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man]] respectively. While the supporting cast is formed by [[Gillian Jacobs]], [[Andrew Rannells]], [[Zazie Beetz]], [[Walton Goggins]], [[Seth Rogen]], [[Sterling K. Brown]], Ross Marquand, [[Malese Jow]], [[Mark Hamill]], [[Chris Diamantopoulos]], [[Kevin Michael Richardson]], [[Fred Tatasciore]], [[Eric Bauza]], [[Jason Mantzoukas]], [[Khary Payton]], [[Zachary Quinto]], [[Grey Griffin]], [[Ben Schwartz]], [[Jay Pharoah]], and [[Calista Flockhart]].

The season was preceded by a special episode, called "Invincible: Atom Eve", which was released on July 21, 2023. The season itself was divided into two parts and premiered on [[Amazon Prime Video]] on November 3, 2023, with the first four episodes each week until November 24, and the final four from March 14, 2024, through April 4. A third season was ordered on April 29, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |date=April 29, 2021 |title='Invincible' Renewed for Season 2 and Season 3 at Amazon |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/invincible-renewed-season-2-amazon-1234963347/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521134013/https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/invincible-renewed-season-2-amazon-1234963347/ |archive-date=May 21, 2021 |access-date=April 29, 2021 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

 |ShortSummary    = Eighteen years ago, government scientist Dr. Elias Brandyworth disobeys his superior, Steven Erickson, and leaves with a dying pregnant woman named Polly, who gives birth to a powerful superhuman. Fulfilling Polly's wishes, Brandyworth swaps her child with the Wilkins' deceased newborn so that she can grow up with a normal family as Samantha Eve Wilkins. Growing up, Eve proves highly knowledgeable about molecules and is admitted to a school for scholars, but longs for a normal life. After discovering her transmutation powers, she is transferred back to public school for failing class. As she attempts to become a hero, she encounters a homeless Brandyworth, who reveals her origins as a government project and warns her not to use her powers. She later battles a group of deformed children that the government created amidst failed attempts at recreating her. After the children die, Erickson captures Eve, Brandyworth, and Polly, intending to use them to create better weapons. In the ensuing fight, Erickson kills Brandyworth and Polly. Enraged, Eve overcomes the mental barrier that prevented her from transmuting living material and erases Erickson's memories. She returns home to find her adoptive parents upset with her for not being normal.

== Production ==
=== Development ===
{{Tweet
| name = Robert Kirkman
| username = Robert Kirkman
| lang = 
| text = Hey  @InvincibleHQ fans! @steveyeun
 & I have some potentially exciting news to share about season 2 and...
| date = Apr 29, 2021
| ID = 1387827848442875905
| reference =

| archive-date = April 29, 2021
| url-status = live
| image = X logo 2023.svg

In April 2021, [[Amazon Prime|Amazon]] and [[Robert Kirkman]], alongside Steven Yeun, announced that ''Invincible'' was renewed for an 8-episode second and third season, which is produced by [[Skybound Entertainment|Skybound]] and executive produced by Kirkman, Simon Racioppa, David Alpert, and [[Catherine Winder]]. Jeff Allen and Linda Lamontagne are serving as the casting director.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joe |first=Otterson |date=Apr 29, 2021 |title=‘Invincible’ Renewed for Seasons 2 and 3 at Amazon |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/invincible-renewed-season-2-amazon-1234963347/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)]]}}</ref>

The concept for the second season was developed during the scripting phase. Some scenes drew partial inspiration from elements in [[Spider-Man]]. Racioppa noted that the [[trilogy]] frequently influenced the writing process. Beyond the visual spectacle of the protagonist’s abilities, [[Sam Raimi|Raimi]]’s films emphasized the internal conflict of [[Spider-Man|Peter Parker]] and the personal consequences of his relationship with [[Mary Jane Watson]].<ref name="Inverse-2024">{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2024 |title='Invincible' Showrunner Breaks Down Season 2's Wild Ending — And Teases Season 3 Plans |url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/invincible-season-2-ending-explained-angstrom-levy-omni-man-season-3? |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Inverse |language=en}}</ref> The season was developed with the intention of presenting new material rather than revisiting earlier storylines, as the first season. The creative team also structured the opening episode to quickly reestablish the series’ intensity, aiming to draw audiences back into the narrative following the gap between seasons.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Dar |first=Taimur |date=2023-10-30 |title=Syndicated Comics |url=https://www.comicsbeat.com/interview-robert-kirkman-and-simon-racioppa-invincible-season-2/ |access-date=2026-03-08 |website=The Beat |language=en-US}}</ref>

Unlike the first season, the second season places greater thematic focus on Mark’s fear of becoming like his father. Rather than concentrating primarily on his development as a superhero, the season explores his anxiety over the possibility that he may share the same nature and ultimately follow a similar path. This concern becomes a central element of his character arc throughout the season.<ref name=":0" />

=== Casting ===
The season featured all series regulars, all of whom returned from the previous season. [[Steven Yeun]] continued to recur as [[Invincible (character)|Invincible]], [[Sandra Oh]] returned to reprising her role as [[Debbie Grayson]]. Actors [[J. K. Simmons]], [[Gillian Jacobs]], [[Zazie Beetz]], and [[Walton Goggins]] also returned during the season, reprising their roles as  [[Omni-Man]], [[Kumiko (character)|Kumiko]], [[Atom Eve]], [[Amber Bennett]], and [[Cecil Stedman]], respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Olivia |date=April 4, 2024 |title=Here's the star-studded voice cast of 'Invincible' and who they play |url=https://africa.businessinsider.com/entertainment/heres-the-star-studded-voice-cast-of-invincible-and-who-they-play/9sdq0de |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=Business Insider Africa |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bojalad |first=Alec |date=November 3, 2023 |title=Invincible Season 2 Cast: Meet the New and Returning Voice Actors |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/invincible-season-2-cast-meet-the-new-and-returning-voice-actors/ |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=Den of Geek |language=en-US}}</ref>

The season also introduces new characters. Among the new characters introduced in the season is [[Angstrom Levy|Sterling K. Brown]], who provides the voice for [[Angstrom Levy]], a [[supervillain]] who has the power of dimensional travel.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Outlaw |first=Kofi |date=2023-09-25 |title=Invincible Season 2 Reveals First Look at Angstrom Levy |url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/invincible-season-2-villains-angstrom-levy-images-first-look-sterling-k-brown/ |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=ComicBook.com |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Jay Pharoah]] is also introduced in the season as Bulletproof, a member of the [[Guardians of the Globe]], who has the power of invincibility and flying. [[Ben Schwartz]] is introduced in the season as [[Shapesmith]], a Martian who has the power of shapeshifting. Other new characters introduced in the season include [[Clancy Brown]], who plays the role of [[General Kregg]], a general in the [[Viltrumite]] army, and [[Shantel VanSanten]], who plays the role of Anissa, a Viltrumite warrior. [[Seth Rogen]] reprises his role as Allen the Alien, while [[Michael Dorn]] reprises his role as [[Battle Beast (Invincible)|Battle Beast]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Every Invincible character you need to remember before Season 3 |url=https://www.dexerto.com/tv-movies/invincible-season-2-cast-characters-voice-actors-2354381/? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[Dexerto]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Writing ===
The writing of the second season continued to follow the character-centric approach that was established in the first season. This was according to Racioppa, the co-showrunner of the series. This approach ensured that the writers explored different ways to reach the key points that were established while ensuring that the overall direction of the season was maintained. The series continued to incorporate elements from the [[Invincible (comics)|comic series]] that was originally written by Kirkman.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=McIntyre |first=Jordan |date=2023-11-03 |title=Exclusive Interview: Simon Racioppa Chats Invincible Season 2! |url=https://multiverseofcolor.com/2023/11/exclusive-interview-invincible-season-2-executive-producer-simon-racioppa-discusses-the-return-of-invincible/ |access-date=2026-03-08 |website=Multiverse Of Color |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Smith-2024">{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Tessa |date=March 13, 2024 |title=Invincible's Simon Racioppa Talks Finding Emotional Balance |url=https://mamasgeeky.com/2024/03/simon-racioppa-invincible-season-2.html? |access-date=February 16, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref> 

The storyline of the second season of the series focuses on the aftermath of the finale of the first season. This season explored the impact that the actions of Omni-Man had on the character of Mark Grayson and Debbie Grayson. The impact of the actions that occurred in the first season was explored realistically. The introduction of new characters to the series continued. This includes the character of Angstrom Levy. This character’s [[multiverse]]-related abilities were explored to ensure that the character’s storyline could be maintained.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Blum-2023">{{Cite web |last=Blum |first=Gillian |date=October 31, 2023 |title=Invincible Season 2 Showrunner Defends Changes from the Comics (Exclusive) |url=https://thedirect.com/article/invincible-season-2-comics-changes-exclusive |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=The Direct |language=en}}</ref>

{{rquote|right|"We're always like, 'What are the real reactions?' or 'What really would happen in the scenario if you had these super-powered characters ... fighting someone who's not superpowered?' Like, they would explode, if [they] got hit. If [[Superman]] punched you, you would explode."|Racioppa  on R-rating scene.}}

The season's [[Motion Picture Association film rating system|R-rating]], received some criticism from viewers, which showrunner Simon Racioppa addressed in a November 2023 interview with ''The Direct''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mercuri |first=Monica |title=When Do New Episodes Of 'Invincible' Season 2 Come Out? The Full Release Schedule For Part 2 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/monicamercuri/2024/03/21/when-do-new-episodes-of-invincible-season-2-come-out-heres-the-full-release-schedule/ |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

Racioppa explained that the increased violence and gore compared to Season 1 were intentional but not gratuitous, emphasizing that [[Character arc|character development]] and narrative conflict remained the primary focus. He noted that this approach allowed the action scenes to escalate naturally, with emotional stakes driving the intensity of the violence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blum |first=Gillian |date=November 21, 2023 |title=Invincible Showrunner Defends Season 2's Most Controversial Decision (Exclusive) |url=https://thedirect.com/article/invincible-season-2-r-rated-scenes-exclusive |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=The Direct |language=en}}</ref>

=== Animation ===
The production faced challenges due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], which caused delays and required the team to rebuild and restart the "factory" of the show.<ref>{{Cite web |last=John |first=Matt |date=September 24, 2023 |title=Invincible Creator Explains Why Season 2 Was Delayed For So Long |url=https://gamerant.com/invincible-season-2-release-date-delay-explained-robert-kirkman/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=Game Rant |language=en}}</ref>

The second season of Invincible mostly consists of hand-drawn 2D animation. The production team reduced the use of [[Computer-generated imagery|CGI]], opting for more [[Traditional animation|traditional hand-drawn animation]] methods. This type of animation was chosen for the show due to the large number of characters in the series and the numerous action-packed scenes. Marge Dean, Head of Animation at [[Skybound Entertainment]], noted, "Quite a lot [of CG animation] was used in Season 1... We still use an element of CG... but, ultimately, the background is drawn into the animation."<ref name="Assistant-2024">{{Cite web |last=Assistant |first=Admin |date=June 18, 2024 |title=FORGING A PARTNERSHIP – AND AN ADULT ANIMATED SERIES – THAT'S INVINCIBLE |url=https://www.vfxvoice.com/forging-a-partnership-and-an-adult-animated-series-thats-invincible/? |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=VFX Voice Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The animation for the show is done in collaboration with studios in [[South Korea]] by Skybound Entertainment. The animation is created through storyboards, animatics, and model sheets. Computer-generated imagery is used minimally for the backgrounds. Other objects in the 2D animation are created through computer-generated imagery.<ref name="Assistant-2024" />

Fight scenes in the show have been complex, as have the destruction of objects and injuries to the characters. Scenes involving the multiverse and Angstrom Levy have been diverse in their settings and color schemes.<ref name="Assistant-2024" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mboho |first=Edidiong |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Robert Kirkman Explains Why 'Invincible' Season 2 Took Over Two Years to Make |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-2-delay-explained-robert-kirkman-comments/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref>

=== Sound and music ===
The [[Sound design|audio design]] of season two was handled by the Boom Box Post team under supervising sound editor Brad Meyer and [[Re-recording mixer|re-recording mixers]] Jeff Shiffman and Jacob Cook and was assisted by several  [[Sound editor (filmmaking)|sound editors]] and foley artists. Season 2 focused on dense immersion audio, with dense, powerful hits for action scenes and close-up sound for calmer scenes. To make superhero combat more substantial, the team laid down an [[Roland TR-808|808 kick drum]] and cannon-style explosions over the hits and added subtle touches like Omni-Man's cape flowing in time with his [[combat]] [[choreography]]. Foley effects were also performed for the series, such as cloth noise, footsteps, and wet sounds, to add realism to action and gore-ridden scenes.<ref name="Walden-2024" />

The crew also created distinctive [[sound effect]]s for [[Telepathy|telepathic]] sequences, including a mental conversation between [[Omni-Man]] and Allen the Alien, and experimented with layered sounds for the techno-organic Viltrumite warriors by adding metal fragments with human-like characteristics to reflect their half-human origin.<ref name="Walden-2024">{{Cite web |last=Walden |first=Jennifer |date=June 14, 2024 |title=Behind the Bold Sound of Animated Series 'Invincible' – with Brad Meyer, Jeff Shiffman, and Jacob Cook |url=https://www.asoundeffect.com/invincible-animation-sound-design/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=A Sound Effect |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Raveena Aurora]] returned to compose the score for the second season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Praveen |date=April 6, 2024 |title=Invincible season 1 & 2 soundtrack: The definitive guide to all songs in the first two seasons |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/comics/invincible-season-1-2-soundtrack-the-definitive-guide-songs-first-two-seasons |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=www.sportskeeda.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, [[The Royals (band)|The Royals]] and [[Radiohead]] were also confirmed to contribute to the soundtrack. The season's [[soundtrack]] features several artists, including Chair Model, Speelburg, Mac Albrecht & [[Orchestre Philharmonique de Strasbourg]], RF Shannon, [[Julianna Barwick]], [[Nick Cave]], [[Blondshell]], [[Zoe Boekbinder]], [[Run the Jewels]], N3W N3W & SYDNY, Olivia Wendel, Bad Nerves, [[Aidan Knight]], Woolly Music, That Kid CG, K-Lab, [[d4vd]], [[Ethel Cain]], [[Fatboy Slim]], and [[Michael Kiwanuka]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Invincible soundtrack: All songs from Seasons 1-3 |url=https://www.dexerto.com/tv-movies/invincible-soundtrack-songs-2389093/? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[Dexerto]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Richards |first=Will |date=November 9, 2023 |title='Invincible' soundtrack: every song in the superhero show |url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/invincible-soundtrack-every-song-in-the-superhero-show-3534984 |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[NME]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Release ==
[[File:Robert_Kirkman_(48410455092).jpg|thumb|[[Robert Kirkman]] At San Diego [[Comic-Con]].]]
The second season of ''Invincible'' was released in two parts on [[Amazon Prime Video]]. The first part premiered on November 3, 2023, with subsequent episodes released weekly until November 24, 2023. The second part began on March 14, 2024, and concluded on April 4, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bradley |first=Russell |last2=Murray |first2=Emily |date=November 1, 2023 |title=How many episodes are in Invincible season 2? |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/invincible-season-2-release-schedule-prime-video-time/? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[GamesRadar+]] |language=en}}</ref> During [[San Diego Comic-Con]] on July 21, 2023, a trailer for the second season was shown, after which it was announced that a special episode, called "Invincible: Atom Eve", would release later that day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 22, 2023 |title=Invincible Gets Standalone Special for Atom Eve Ahead of Season 2 |url=https://www.cbr.com/invincible-atom-eve-prime-video-special/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729121935/https://www.cbr.com/invincible-atom-eve-prime-video-special/ |archive-date=July 29, 2023 |access-date=July 29, 2023 |website=CBR |language=en}}</ref>

The show experienced a mid-season hiatus,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invincible Season 2 Goes On Mid-Winter Break {{!}} Cosmic Book News |url=https://cosmicbook.news/invincible-season-2-goes-on-mid-winter-break |access-date=October 24, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref> a move that was not part of the original production plan. Co-showrunner Simon Racioppa confirmed that this pause was necessitated by release setbacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Power |first=Tom |date=October 31, 2023 |title='Wasn't the original plan': Invincible co-showrunner explains why season 2 is releasing in two parts |url=https://www.techradar.com/streaming/amazon-prime-video/wasnt-the-original-plan-invincible-showrunner-explains-why-season-2-is-releasing-in-two-parts? |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=[[TechRadar]] |language=en}}</ref> Adding a creative layer to the decision, creator Robert Kirkman revealed that the mid-season break was also deliberately planned around the holiday season. This allowed viewers time to reflect on the main plot developments and ensured the show would maintain visibility during a period saturated with many other major new releases.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Mike |date=January 22, 2023 |title='Invincible' Season 2 Part 2: Release Date, Trailer, and Everything We Know So Far |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-2-updates-release-window-trailer-cast-plot/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=John |first=Matt |date=August 2, 2023 |title=Invincible Creator Reveals The Real Reason Why Season 2 Takes A Mid-Season Break |url=https://gamerant.com/invincible-season-2-midseason-break-explained-robert-kirkman/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=[[Game Rant]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Volk |first=Pete |date=October 15, 2024 |title=Invincible season 3 teaser promises no mid-season break this time |url=https://www.polygon.com/tv/465898/invincible-season-3-date-teaser-no-midseason-break |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Because the show was airing weekly, a strategy used to promote subscriptions to Amazon Prime Video, a delay in its initial starting date would have pushed the final four episodes into the Christmas period. Amazon sought to avoid this overlap so they could instead focus on promoting their slate of original Christmas films and shows.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demegillo |first=Manuel |date=March 13, 2024 |title=Invincible Producer Explains Season 2 Delay |url=https://www.cbr.com/invincible-season-2-delay/ |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=CBR |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Rourke |first=Ryan |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Robert Kirkman Explains Why 'Invincible' Season 2 Was Split Into Two Parts |url=https://collider.com/invincible-season-2-two-part-release-robert-kirkman-comments/ |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Audience viewership ===
Viewership data for the second season increased substantially compared to its first season, with reports indicating that the season premiere attracted approximately three times the opening weekend audience of the first season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulatowski |first=Rachel |date=November 12, 2023 |title=Invincible Season 2 Premiere Breaks Season 1's Viewership Record (& It's By A Lot) |url=https://screenrant.com/invincible-season-2-premiere-viewership-record-season-1-comparison/? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[Screen Rant]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Critical response ===
The [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]] calculated that 100% approval rating based on 42 reviews were positive and the average rating for the season was 8.4 out of 10. The website's critics consensus reads, "Still as bracing as a punch to the face and invigorating with its vivid worldbuilding, ''Invincible'' is practically impervious to disappointing audiences in this sterling sophomore season."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invincible: Season 2 {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/invincible/s02? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |language=en}}</ref>

''Invincible season 2''<nowiki/>'s second season received generally positive responses. Logan Moore of ''[[ComicBook.com]]'' notes, "Invincible continues to be one of the best and most unique superhero shows around."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Logan |date=October 30, 2023 |title=Invincible Season 2 – Part 1 Review: Well Worth the Long Wait |url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/invincible-season-2-part-1-review-well-worth-the-wait/ |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Screen Rant]]''<nowiki/>'s Cooper Hood described ''Invincible'' Season 2 as "worth the wait" However, he criticized the split release for creating uneven pacing and found the use of [[Angstrom Levy]] as the main antagonist in Part 1 somewhat disappointing.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hood |first=Cooper |date=October 30, 2023 |title=Invincible Season 2 - Part 1 Review: The Best Superhero Show Is Back & Worth The Wait |url=https://screenrant.com/invincible-season-2-part-1-review/ |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=[[Screen Rant]] |language=en}}</ref> 

Leila Latif of ''[[The Guardian]]'' gave the season five out of five stars, describing it as “the best superhero show on television.” She praised its character development, writing, and animation, calling it “a triumph” for its performances, humor, and action.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Latif |first=Leila |date=November 3, 2023 |title=Invincible review – far and away the best superhero show on TV |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/nov/03/invincible-season-two-review-television-amazon-prime-video |access-date=February 18, 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Saloni Gajjar of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' wrote that Season 2, Part 2 features strong action and key plot developments appealing to both new viewers and comic fans. She commended the animation and its balance between violence and character-driven storytelling, noting Mark Grayson’s continued moral struggles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invincible season 2, part 2 review: A bloody good time |url=https://www.avclub.com/tv-review-invincible-season-2-part-2-prime-video |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Charles Pulliam-Moore, of ''[[The Verge]]'', reviewed the second season of ''Invincible'' as a thoughtful step toward a bigger universe. In his review, Pulliam-Moore discusses how the season aligns with [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]'s current interest in [[multiverse]] narratives, while staying true to its [[Invincible (comics)|comic book]] origins. He notes that the series expands its universe thoughtfully, introducing new characters and plotlines that enrich the overarching story. Pulliam-Moore also comments on the show's animation quality and its approach to balancing action with character development. Overall, he views the second season as a significant progression that sets the stage for future developments in the series.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pulliam-Moore |first=Charles |date=October 30, 2023 |title=Invincible season 2 is a thoughtful step toward a bigger universe |url=https://www.theverge.com/23933816/invincible-season-2-review |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=[[The Verge]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Sam Stone of ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' gave season 9 a grade of out of 10, appreciating more emphasis on emotional character development, especially the trauma and guilt of [[Invincible (character)|Mark Grayson]] following the first season. He also mentioned its responsibility and heroism cost themes compared to [[Spider-Man]]'s storyline. Stone also stated that he appreciated the animation, the voice acting, and the fuller character development, and felt that the season achieves the action and emotion in proportion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stone |first=Sam |date=November 3, 2023 |title=REVIEW: Invincible Season 2 Heightens the Emotional Stakes |url=https://www.cbr.com/invincible-season-2-review/ |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |language=en}}</ref> 

''[[IGN]]''<nowiki/>'s reviewed Siddhant Adlakha noted its depth of emotion and character development in the season, praising how its combination of action and introspection delivered something different. He listed dynamics among [[Omni-Man|Nolan]], [[Debbie Grayson|Debbie]], and Mark as one of the season's strongest points and felt that despite some unbalanced moments in the story, it worked best when trying to balance the family dynamics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adlakha |first=Siddhant |date=April 5, 2024 |title=Invincible Season 2 Review |url=https://za.ign.com/invincible-season-2/192542/review/invincible-season-2-review |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=IGN Africa |language=en-za}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
[[Sterling K. Brown]] received a nomination for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance|Outstanding Character Voice-Over Performance]] at the [[76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]] for his portrayal of Angstrom Levy in the episode "[[I Thought You Were Stronger]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Invincible |url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/shows/invincible |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=Television Academy |language=en}}</ref>

Additionally, the season was nominated for [[Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Animated Series|Best Animated Series]] at the 2025 [[Critics' Choice Television Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=See all the winners at the 2025 Critics Choice Awards |url=https://ew.com/critics-choice-awards-2025-winners-list-8770855? |access-date=February 13, 2025 |website=EW.com |language=en}}</ref> The series also earned a nomination for Outstanding Achievement for Storyboarding in an Animated Television/Broadcast Production at the [[52nd Annie Awards|2025 Annie Awards]].
